Details: This example creates an in-memory SQLite database with departments, employees, and projects. Foreign keys connect employees to departments and projects to their leads, ensuring each reference points to an existing row. Sample data includes an empty department, employees without projects, and a lead with multiple projects to show different join outcomes. INNER JOIN matches employees to departments and links projects through their leads to departments. LEFT JOIN keeps all departments or employees even when no related row exists, and IS NULL identifies employees without a project. The query results below show these relationships before the temporary database is closed.
Database contents: 4 departments, 8 employees, and 5 projects.
Employees who do not lead projects: Bob Martinez, Emma Garcia, Frank Wilson, Henry Patel.
Employees leading multiple projects: Alice Park (2).

No database fixes were needed or applied. The empty department and employees without projects are intentional sample cases, not necessarily errors. Foreign-key checks were enabled to prevent invalid department and project-lead references, and missing matches are clearly labeled in the results.
